questions.q: Identify the Indian classical dancer associated with Kathak.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Rohini Bhate.

Key Points

• Rohini Bhate was an eminent Indian classical dancer renowned for her expertise in the Kathak dance form.

• She was a disciple of Guru Lachhu Maharaj and Shambhu Maharaj, both legendary exponents of Kathak.

• Her dance style was characterized by its technical precision and expressive storytelling.

• She was also a respected teacher and choreographer, contributing significantly to the propagation and evolution of Kathak.

Additional Information

• Kathak

• Kathak is one of the eight major forms of Indian classical dance.

• It originated from the nomadic bards of ancient northern India, known as Kathakars or storytellers.

• The dance form emphasizes intricate footwork, spins, and expressive gestures to convey stories, often from epics like the Mahabharata and Ramayana.

• Kathak has three main gharanas (schools) - Lucknow, Jaipur, and Banaras, each with its unique style and emphasis.

• Other Indian Classical Dance Forms

• Bharatanatyam - Originating from Tamil Nadu, it is known for its fixed upper torso, bent legs, and intricate footwork combined with expressive hand gestures and facial expressions.

• Kathakali - A dance-drama from Kerala, characterized by elaborate costumes, detailed gestures, and well-defined body movements presented in the form of a story-play.

• Kuchipudi - Hailing from Andhra Pradesh, it blends fast rhythms and fluid movements with dramatic storytelling.

• Odissi - From Odisha, it is known for its grace, fluid movements, and sculpturesque poses.

• Manipuri - A dance form from Manipur, characterized by smooth and graceful movements, often depicting themes from the life of Lord Krishna.

• Mohiniyattam - A classical dance from Kerala, it combines elements of Bharatanatyam and Kathakali, performed by women with slow, graceful movements.

• Sattriya - Originating from Assam, it is a dance-drama that combines dance, drama, and music.

questions.q: British Parliament introduced Indian High Courts Act in which year?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 1861.

Key Points

• The Indian High Courts Act was introduced by the British Parliament in the year 1861.

• This act led to the establishment of High Courts in India for the first time, replacing the older Supreme Courts at Calcutta, Bombay, and Madras.

• The High Courts were given extensive original and appellate jurisdiction, marking a significant shift in the Indian judicial system.

• These High Courts were modeled after the English judicial system and were intended to provide a higher level of judicial administration in the major cities of India.

Additional Information

• Indian High Courts Act 1861

• The Indian High Courts Act 1861 was an act of the British Parliament that led to the creation of High Courts in India in the three Presidency towns of Calcutta, Bombay, and Madras.

• Before this act, the judicial system in these cities was managed by Supreme Courts, which were established under the Charter Act of 1774.

• The new High Courts were granted original civil and criminal jurisdiction, appellate jurisdiction, and supervisory jurisdiction over the lower courts.

• This act was significant as it brought uniformity and improvement in the judicial administration of British India.

• Supreme Courts of Calcutta, Bombay, and Madras

• These courts were established under the Regulating Act of 1773 and subsequent acts, and they functioned until the High Courts were established in 1861.

• They were the highest courts in British India and had both original and appellate jurisdiction.

• The Supreme Courts were replaced by the High Courts to streamline and improve the judicial system.

• Judicial Administration in British India

• The British introduced several reforms to the judicial system in India to make it more efficient and aligned with British legal principles.

• The High Courts Act was a part of these reforms, which aimed to enhance the administration of justice in the colonies.

• These reforms were crucial in shaping the modern Indian judicial system.

questions.q: In which of the following years was the Election Commission of India founded?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 1950.

Key Points

• The Election Commission of India (ECI) was established on 25th January 1950.

• It is an autonomous constitutional authority responsible for administering election processes in India at both the national and state levels.

• The ECI ensures the conduct of free and fair elections in the country, which is a fundamental aspect of the democratic framework of India.

• The Election Commission operates under the authority of the Constitution per Article 324, and subsequently enacted Representation of the People Acts.

Additional Information

• Election Commission of India (ECI)

• The ECI is responsible for the superintendence, direction, and control of the preparation of the electoral rolls for, and the conduct of, all elections to Parliament and to the Legislature of every State and of elections to the offices of President and Vice President held under the Constitution.

• The body administers elections to the Lok Sabha, Rajya Sabha, and State Legislative Assemblies in India, and the offices of the President and Vice President in the country.

• It was originally a one-member body but was made a three-member body in 1989.

• The Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) heads the Election Commission of India.

• Article 324 of the Indian Constitution

• Article 324 vests the power of superintendence, direction, and control of elections in an independent body, which is the Election Commission.

• The Election Commission has the power to take all necessary steps to ensure free and fair elections.

• Representation of the People Acts

• The Representation of the People Act, 1950 provides for the allocation of seats in the House of the People and in the Legislative Assemblies, the delimitation of constituencies for elections, the qualifications of voters at such elections, and other related matters.

• The Representation of the People Act, 1951 provides for the actual conduct of elections in India, the qualifications and disqualifications for membership of Parliament and State Legislatures, and the resolution of election disputes.

questions.q: In Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi Yojana, beneficiaries are provided with how much amount every year?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is ₹6,000.

Key Points

• The Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi Yojana (PM-Kisan) is a central sector scheme launched by the Government of India.

• Under this scheme, income support of ₹6,000 per year is provided to all farmer families across the country.

• This amount is paid in three equal installments of ₹2,000 each, which are directly transferred to the bank accounts of the beneficiaries.

• The scheme aims to support the financial needs of farmers in procuring various inputs to ensure proper crop health and appropriate yields.

Additional Information

• Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi (PM-Kisan)

• PM-Kisan is a central sector scheme with 100% funding from the Government of India.

• It was launched on 24th February 2019, and the first installment was paid out in December 2018.

• The scheme is implemented by the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare.

• All landholding farmer families are eligible for this scheme, provided they meet the criteria set by the government.

• Objectives

• The main objective of PM-Kisan is to provide financial support to farmers, helping them to procure various inputs for agriculture and allied activities, as well as domestic needs.

• The scheme aims to supplement the financial needs of the farmers in procuring inputs for crop production, ensuring proper crop health and yields.

• It also aims to protect farmers from falling into the clutches of moneylenders for meeting such expenses and ensure their continuance in farming activities.

• Eligibility Criteria

• All landholding farmer families, which have cultivable landholding in their names, are eligible for this scheme.

• However, certain exclusions apply, such as institutional landholders, farmer families holding constitutional posts, serving or retired officers and employees of state/central government as well as public sector undertakings and government autonomous bodies, and professionals like doctors, engineers, and lawyers.

• Implementation

• The scheme is implemented through an electronic database containing the details of all the beneficiaries.

• The funds are directly transferred to the bank accounts of the beneficiaries through Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) mode.

• The states and union territories are responsible for identifying the farmer families which are eligible for support as per scheme guidelines.

questions.q: When was pro kabaddi league inaugurated for the first time in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 2014.

Key Points

• The Pro Kabaddi League was inaugurated for the first time in India in 2014.

• It was established with the aim to popularize the sport of kabaddi and provide a professional platform for players.

• The league was inspired by the success of the kabaddi tournament at the 2006 Asian Games.

• The inaugural season of the Pro Kabaddi League featured eight teams, which competed in a double round-robin format followed by playoffs.

Additional Information

• Pro Kabaddi League (PKL)

• The Pro Kabaddi League is a professional-level kabaddi league in India, established in 2014.

• It is organized by Mashal Sports and STAR India, with the backing of the Amateur Kabaddi Federation of India (AKFI), the Asian Kabaddi Federation (AKF), and the International Kabaddi Federation (IKF).

• The league follows a format similar to that of the Indian Premier League (IPL), with franchises representing various cities across India.

• Players from different countries, including Iran, South Korea, and Kenya, participate in the league, making it a global event.

• The league has significantly contributed to the growth and popularity of kabaddi, both in India and internationally.

• Kabaddi

• Kabaddi is a contact team sport that originated in ancient India.

• The game involves two teams of seven players each, who take turns sending a "raider" into the opposing team's half of the court to tag as many defenders as possible and return to their half of the court without being tackled.

• Points are scored by the raider for each defender tagged, while the opposing team earns points for stopping the raider.

• Kabaddi is known for its fast-paced and physically demanding nature, requiring strength, agility, and strategic thinking.

questions.q: Wood’s Dispatch of 1854 primarily dealt with which of the following subject matters?
questions.solution:

Key Points

• Wood's Dispatch of 1854 is considered the Magna Carta of English Education in India.

• The Dispatch recommended a system of education from the primary level to the university level.

• It proposed the establishment of universities in major cities like Bombay, Calcutta, and Madras.

• Wood's Dispatch emphasized the need for vocational and female education.

Additional Information

• Wood's Dispatch

• Wood's Dispatch was a comprehensive plan for the education system in India, formulated by Sir Charles Wood, the President of the Board of Control of the British East India Company, in 1854.

• It laid the foundation for a systematic and organized education policy in India under British rule.

• The Dispatch recommended the establishment of a Department of Public Instruction in each province to oversee education matters.

• It also suggested the use of vernacular languages at the primary level, while English was to be the medium of instruction for higher education.

• Universities in Major Cities

• Following the recommendations of Wood's Dispatch, universities were established in Bombay, Calcutta, and Madras in 1857.

• These universities played a crucial role in shaping modern education in India and produced many notable scholars and leaders.

• Vocational and Female Education

• Wood's Dispatch emphasized the importance of vocational education to improve the skills of the workforce.

• It also highlighted the need for female education to uplift the status of women in society.

• Special grants were recommended to promote female education.

questions.q: The tropical cyclones in Australia are known as .
questions.solution:

Key Points

• Willy-willies is the term used to describe tropical cyclones in Australia.

• Tropical cyclones are intense low-pressure systems that form over warm ocean waters and can cause significant damage to coastal regions.

• These cyclones are characterized by strong winds, heavy rainfall, and can lead to flooding and storm surges.

• The term willy-willies is specifically used in the Australian region, whereas other regions have different terms for similar weather phenomena.

Additional Information

• Hurricanes

• Hurricanes are tropical cyclones that occur in the North Atlantic Ocean and northeastern Pacific Ocean.

• The term is used primarily in the Caribbean Sea, Gulf of Mexico, and along the eastern coastlines of the United States and Mexico.

• They are known for their destructive power, which includes strong winds, heavy rains, and storm surges.

• Typhoons

• Typhoons are tropical cyclones that occur in the northwestern Pacific Ocean, primarily affecting Southeast Asia, Japan, and eastern China.

• They are similar in structure and impact to hurricanes and willy-willies, with strong winds and heavy rainfall.

• The term "typhoon" is derived from the Chinese term "tai fung," meaning "great wind."

• Cyclones

• The term "cyclone" is a general term used to describe a rotating, organized system of clouds and thunderstorms that originate over tropical or subtropical waters.

• In the Indian Ocean and South Pacific, these systems are referred to as cyclones.

• Cyclones can cause extensive damage, including high winds, heavy rainfall, and coastal flooding.

questions.q: If GNP is 16% higher than the last year and the rate of inflation is 9%, production in the economy has grown by:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 0.07.

Key Points

• The Gross National Product (GNP) is a broad measure of a nation's total economic activity.

• The GNP is 16% higher than the last year, indicating overall economic growth.

• Inflation rate is 9%, which represents the rate at which the general level of prices for goods and services is rising.

• The production growth rate can be determined by adjusting the GNP growth rate for inflation.

Additional Information

• Gross National Product (GNP)

• GNP measures the market value of all the products and services produced in one year by labor and property supplied by the residents of a country.

• It includes the value of goods and services produced by a country's residents, regardless of the location of the actual production.

• Inflation

• Inflation is the rate at which the general level of prices for goods and services is rising and subsequently eroding purchasing power.

• Central banks attempt to limit inflation, and avoid deflation, in order to keep the economy running smoothly.

• Economic Growth

• Economic growth is an increase in the production of economic goods and services, compared from one period of time to another.

• It can be measured in nominal or real terms, the latter of which is adjusted for inflation.

• Calculation of Production Growth Rate

• To find the production growth rate, we adjust the GNP growth rate for inflation.

• Formula: Production Growth Rate = (1 + GNP Growth Rate) / (1 + Inflation Rate) - 1

• Using the given values: GNP Growth Rate = 16% or 0.16, Inflation Rate = 9% or 0.09

• Production Growth Rate = (1 + 0.16) / (1 + 0.09) - 1 = 1.16 / 1.09 - 1 = 1.0642 - 1 ≈ 0.07

questions.q: Akshara and Siddharth travel from point P to Q, a distance of 72 km at a rate of 8 km/h and 10 km/h, respectively. Siddharth reaches Q first and returns immediately and meets Akshara at R. Find the distance from P to R.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

When two persons start together from a point, and one reaches the destination and returns to meet the other, the total distance covered by both is 2 × Distance between the points.

Total distance covered = 2 × 72 = 144 km.

Ratio of distances covered = Ratio of their speeds = 8 : 10 = 4 : 5.

Distance covered by Akshara (PR) = (4 ÷ 9) × 144 = 64 km.

∴ The correct answer is 64 km.

Alternate Method

Given:

Distance between P and Q = 72 km

Speed of Akshara = 8 km/h

Speed of Siddharth = 10 km/h



Formula Used:

Distance = Speed × Time

Total distance covered by both = 2 × Distance between two points

Calculations:

⇒ Let the time taken for them to meet at point R be 't' hours.

⇒ Distance covered by Akshara in t hours = PR = 8t km

⇒ Distance covered by Siddharth in t hours = PQ + QR = 10t km

⇒ The sum of the distances covered by both = PR + PQ + QR

⇒ Since PR + QR = PQ, the total distance covered = 2 × PQ = 2 × 72 = 144 km.

⇒ 8t + 10t = 144

⇒ 18t = 144

⇒ t = 8 hours

⇒ Distance from P to R = 8t = 8 × 8 = 64 km

∴ The correct answer is 64 km.

Additional Information

Meeting Point Concept

When two individuals start simultaneously from point A towards B, and the faster one returns immediately from B to meet the slower one at C, the total distance covered by both is exactly twice the distance between A and B (2D).

Direct Distance Ratio

Since the time of travel until they meet is constant for both, the distance covered is directly proportional to their respective speeds. Thus, Distance Ratio = S₁ : S₂.

questions.q: In a collection of rare coins, there is one gold coin for every four non-gold coins. If 20 more gold coins are added to the collection, the ratio of the number of gold coins to that of non-gold coins will be 2:3. The total number of coins in the collection will now become _.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Initial Ratio (Gold : Non-Gold) = 1 : 4 = 3 : 12

New Ratio (Gold : Non-Gold) = 2 : 3 = 8 : 12 (Non-Gold parts made equal)

Increase in Gold parts = 8 − 3 = 5 parts

Given 5 parts = 20 coins ⇒ 1 part = 4 coins

Total new parts = 8 + 12 = 20 parts ⇒ New total coins = 20 × 4 = 80 coins

∴ The correct answer is 80 coins.

Alternate Method

Given:

Initial ratio of gold to non-gold coins = 1 : 4

Number of gold coins added = 20

New ratio of gold to non-gold coins = 2 : 3

Formula / Logic Used:

Since the number of non-gold coins remains unchanged, we can equate the number of non-gold coins in both cases to simplify the calculation.



Calculations:

⇒ Let the initial number of gold coins be x and non-gold coins be 4x.

⇒ After adding 20 gold coins, new number of gold coins = x + 20

⇒ Number of non-gold coins remains 4x.

⇒ New ratio = (x + 20) ÷ 4x = 2 ÷ 3

⇒ Cross-multiplying: 3(x + 20) = 2 × 4x

⇒ 3x + 60 = 8x

⇒ 8x − 3x = 60

⇒ 5x = 60

⇒ x = 12

⇒ New total number of coins = (x + 20) + 4x = 5x + 20

⇒ Total coins = 5 × 12 + 20 = 60 + 20 = 80

∴ The correct answer is 80 coins.

Additional Information

Making Parts Equal

When a mixture or collection changes due to the addition of only one component, making the ratio parts of the unchanged component equal across both ratios provides a direct unit-based solution without requiring basic algebra equations.

Cross-Multiplication Method

If an initial ratio a : b transforms to c : d by adding x and y respectively, it can be directly solved using the algebraic relationship: (a + x) ÷ (b + y) = c ÷ d.

Compound Ratio

The compound ratio of two or more given ratios is the product of their corresponding antecedents (first terms) and consequents (second terms). For example, the compound ratio of a : b and c : d is ac : bd.

⇒ Now, check for the divisibility by 3.

⇒ Sum of the digits = 2 + 4 + 9 + k + 8 + 7 + 6

⇒ Sum of the digits = 36 + k

⇒ We need the expression (36 + k) to be a multiple of 3.

⇒ Since 36 is exactly divisible by 3, the possible single-digit values of k are 0, 3, 6, and 9.

⇒ The question asks for the least value of k.

⇒ The least possible value among the options is 0.

∴ The correct answer is 0.

Additional Information

Divisibility Rule of 3

A number is divisible by 3 if the sum of all its digits is completely divisible by 3.

Divisibility Rule of 4

A number is divisible by 4 if the number formed by its last two digits is divisible by 4.

Divisibility Rule of 8

A number is divisible by 8 if the number formed by its last three digits is divisible by 8.

Divisibility Rule of 9

A number is divisible by 9 if the sum of all its digits is completely divisible by 9.

Divisibility Rule of 11

A number is divisible by 11 if the difference between the sum of digits at odd positions and the sum of digits at even positions is 0 or a multiple of 11.

7200 × 16 × 3 = 9600 × x × 4

Principal 2 (P₂) = ₹9,600, Rate 2 (R₂) = x%, Time 2 (T₂) = 4 years

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100



Calculations:

⇒ SI₁ = (7200 × 16 × 3) ÷ 100

⇒ SI₂ = (9600 × x × 4) ÷ 100

According to the question, SI₁ = SI₂

⇒ (7200 × 16 × 3) ÷ 100 = (9600 × x × 4) ÷ 100

⇒ 72 × 48 = 96 × 4x

⇒ 3456 = 384x

⇒ x = 3456 ÷ 384

⇒ x = 9

∴ The correct answer is 9%.

Additional Information

Simple Interest (SI)

It is the interest calculated strictly on the initial principal amount throughout the entire period. The formula used is SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100.

Constant Interest Concept

When the simple interest obtained from two different investments is completely equal, their respective (P × R × T) products must balance out equally.

Amount

The amount refers to the total final sum of the principal and the simple interest earned over the given duration. Formula: A = P + SI = P(1 + (R × T) ÷ 100).

questions.q: If a shopkeeper sells sugar at ₹44.8 per kg, he is able to make a 12% profit. Due to water seepage, 51​ of the sugar is damaged. What should now be the selling price per kg of the rest of the sugar to have a 5% profit?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Cost Price (CP) per kg = Selling Price ÷ (1 + Profit%) = 44.8 ÷ 1.12 = ₹40.

To gain a 5% overall profit, the target revenue per kg of initial stock must be 40 × 1.05 = ₹42.

Since 1/5 of the sugar is damaged, only 4/5 of the quantity remains to be sold.

The entire target revenue must be generated by the remaining sugar.

New Selling Price per kg = Target Revenue ÷ Remaining Fraction = 42 ÷ (4/5) = 42 × 5 ÷ 4 = ₹52.5.

∴ The correct answer is ₹52.5.

Alternate Method

Given:

Selling Price (SP) of sugar = ₹44.8 per kg

Initial profit = 12%

Damaged portion = 1/5 of the total sugar

Target overall profit = 5%

Formula Used:

Cost Price = Selling Price ÷ (1 + Profit/100)

Total Selling Price = Total Cost Price × (1 + Desired Profit/100)



Calculations:

⇒ Let the total quantity of sugar be 5 kg.

⇒ Cost Price (CP) per kg = 44.8 ÷ 1.12 = ₹40

⇒ Total CP for 5 kg = 5 × 40 = ₹200

⇒ Since 5% overall profit is required, target Total SP = 200 × 1.05 = ₹210

⇒ Quantity of damaged sugar = 1/5 of 5 kg = 1 kg (yields ₹0 revenue)

⇒ Remaining quantity to be sold = 5 − 1 = 4 kg

⇒ New Selling Price per kg = Target Total SP ÷ Remaining Quantity

⇒ New SP per kg = 210 ÷ 4 = ₹52.5

∴ The correct answer is ₹52.5.

Additional Information

Cost Price and Selling Price Relation

When profit is made, SP = CP × (100 + Profit%) ÷ 100. For loss, SP = CP × (100 − Loss%) ÷ 100.

Impact of Damaged Goods on Profit

Goods that are completely damaged yield zero revenue. This effectively acts as a 100% loss on that specific portion, meaning the remaining goods must be sold at a higher markup to achieve the target overall profit.

Weighted Average in Profit & Loss

If quantity is split into parts (e.g., Q₁ and Q₂) sold at profit % P₁ and P₂, overall profit % = (Q₁P₁ + Q₂P₂) ÷ (Q₁ + Q₂). For completely damaged goods, P = −100%.

questions.q: For what value of k, the system of equations kx - 15y + 7 = 0 and 7x - 21y - 19 = 0 has NO solution?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

For a system of linear equations to have no solution, the ratio of x-coefficients must equal the ratio of y-coefficients.

a₁ / a₂ = b₁ / b₂

k / 7 = −15 / −21

k = 7 × (5 / 7) = 5

∴ The correct answer is 5.

Alternate Method

Given:

Equation 1: kx − 15y + 7 = 0

Equation 2: 7x − 21y − 19 = 0

Formula Used:

For two linear equations a₁x + b₁y + c₁ = 0 and a₂x + b₂y + c₂ = 0 to have NO solution, the condition is:

a₁ / a₂ = b₁ / b₂ ≠ c₁ / c₂

Calculations:

⇒ Comparing the given equations with the standard form, we get:

⇒ a₁ = k, b₁ = −15, c₁ = 7

⇒ a₂ = 7, b₂ = −21, c₂ = −19

⇒ Applying the condition for no solution:

⇒ k / 7 = (−15) / (−21)

⇒ k / 7 = 15 / 21

⇒ k / 7 = 5 / 7

⇒ k = 5

⇒ Checking the second part of the condition:

⇒ b₁ / b₂ = 5 / 7

⇒ c₁ / c₂ = 7 / (−19)

⇒ 5 / 7 ≠ −7 / 19 (Condition satisfied)

∴ The correct answer is 5.

Additional Information

Condition for Unique Solution (Intersecting Lines)

The system of equations has exactly one solution if a₁ / a₂ ≠ b₁ / b₂.

Condition for Infinitely Many Solutions (Coincident Lines)

The system has infinitely many solutions if all ratios are equal: a₁ / a₂ = b₁ / b₂ = c₁ / c₂.

Condition for No Solution (Parallel Lines)

The system has no solution if the lines are strictly parallel: a₁ / a₂ = b₁ / b₂ ≠ c₁ / c₂.

questions.q: Find the measure of the central angle of a sector if its area is 16π and the radius is 8.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Total area of the circle = π × r² = π × 8² = 64π

Area of the sector is given as 16π.

Ratio of sector area to total area = 16π ÷ 64π = 1/4

Central angle = (1/4) × 360° = 90°

∴ The correct answer is 90°.

Alternate Method

Given:

Area of the sector = 16π

Radius (r) = 8

Formula Used:

Area of a sector = (θ ÷ 360°) × πr²



Calculations:

⇒ 16π = (θ ÷ 360°) × π × (8)²

⇒ 16π = (θ ÷ 360°) × 64π

⇒ 16 ÷ 64 = θ ÷ 360°

⇒ 1/4 = θ ÷ 360°

⇒ θ = 360° ÷ 4 = 90°

∴ The correct answer is 90°.

Additional Information

Length of an Arc

The length of an arc of a sector with central angle θ is given by l = (θ ÷ 360°) × 2πr.

Perimeter of a Sector

The perimeter of a sector includes the arc length and the two radii: P = l + 2r.

Area of a Segment

The area of the segment enclosed by a chord and its corresponding arc is determined by subtracting the area of the triangle formed by the radii and the chord from the area of the sector.

⇒ Area of ΔABC = 25 × 3.87 = 96.75 cm²

Base of right ΔPQR = √(13² − 12²) = 5 cm

⇒ Area of ΔPQR = &21​ × 12 × 5 = 30 cm²

∴ The correct answer is 66.75 cm².

Alternate Method

Given:

Sides of ΔABC are 10 cm, 20 cm, and 20 cm.

In ΔPQR, hypotenuse = 13 cm, one perpendicular side = 12 cm.

Formula Used:

Heron's Formula for Area = √(s(s − a)(s − b)(s − c))

Pythagorean Theorem: Hypotenuse² = Perpendicular² + Base²

Area of right triangle = &21​ × Base × Height



Calculations:

⇒ Semi-perimeter of ΔABC, s = (10 + 20 + 20) ÷ 2 = 50 ÷ 2 = 25 cm

⇒ Area of ΔABC = √(25 × (25 − 10) × (25 − 20) × (25 − 20))

⇒ Area of ΔABC = √(25 × 15 × 5 × 5) = √(9375) = 25√15 cm²

⇒ Given √15 ≈ 3.87, Area = 25 × 3.87 = 96.75 cm²

⇒ In right ΔPQR, Base = √(13² − 12²) = √(169 − 144) = √25 = 5 cm

⇒ Area of ΔPQR = &21​ × 12 × 5 = 30 cm²

Additional Information

Heron's Formula

Used to find the area of a general triangle when all three sides are known: Area = √(s(s−a)(s−b)(s−c)), where s = (a+b+c) ÷ 2.

Pythagorean Theorem

For any right-angled triangle, the square of the hypotenuse equals the sum of squares of perpendicular and base: H² = P² + B².

Area of an Isosceles Triangle

Can also be calculated using the direct formula: Area = (b ÷ 4) × √(4a² − b²), where 'a' is the length of equal sides and 'b' is the base.

questions.q: At what angle is the arc length half the perimeter of the circle?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

The total perimeter (circumference) of a circle corresponds to a complete central angle of 360°.

Since the arc length is exactly half of the total perimeter, the corresponding angle will also be exactly half.

⇒ Required Angle = 360° ÷ 2

⇒ Required Angle = 180°

∴ The correct answer is 180°.

Alternate Method



Given:

Arc length = 1/2 × Perimeter of the circle

Formula Used:

Perimeter of a circle = 2πr

Arc length = (θ ÷ 360°) × 2πr

Calculation:

⇒ Arc length = 1/2 × 2πr

⇒ Arc length = πr

Equating this to the arc length formula:

⇒ (θ ÷ 360°) × 2πr = πr

⇒ θ ÷ 360° = πr ÷ 2πr

⇒ θ ÷ 360° = 1/2

⇒ θ = 1/2 × 360°

⇒ θ = 180°

∴ The correct answer is 180°.

Additional Information

Area of a Sector

The area of a sector with central angle θ is directly proportional to its angle and is given by (θ ÷ 360°) × πr².

Perimeter of a Semicircular Region

While the curved arc length of a semicircle is πr, the total perimeter of a closed semicircular region includes the straight diameter as well, making it πr + 2r.

Quadrant of a Circle

A quadrant represents one-fourth of a circle with a central angle of 90°. Its curved arc length is πr ÷ 2.

questions.q: In a company, all employees are getting equal wages. If the number of employees is increased by 20% and their wages per head are decreased by 18%, what is the percentage decrease in total wages?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

When a value is a product of two variables, the net percentage change can be found using the successive percentage formula: x + y + (x × y)/100

Here, the number of employees increased by 20% (x = 20) and wages decreased by 18% (y = −18).

Net Change = 20 − 18 + [(20 × −18) / 100]

Net Change = 2 − 3.6 = −1.6%

The negative sign clearly indicates a total decrease in wages.

∴ The correct answer is 1.6%.

Alternate Method

Given:

Increase in number of employees = 20%

Decrease in wages per head = 18%

Formula Used:

Total Wages = Number of Employees × Wages per head

Percentage Change = [(Final Value − Initial Value) / Initial Value] × 100



Calculations:

Let the initial number of employees be 100 and the wage per head be 100.

⇒ Initial Total Wages = 100 × 100 = 10000

⇒ New number of employees = 100 + 20% of 100 = 120

⇒ New wage per head = 100 − 18% of 100 = 82

⇒ Final Total Wages = 120 × 82 = 9840

⇒ Decrease in Total Wages = 10000 − 9840 = 160

⇒ Percentage Decrease = (160 / 10000) × 100 = 1.6%

∴ The correct answer is 1.6%.

Additional Information

Successive Percentage Formula

When a quantity undergoes two consecutive percentage changes x and y, the net change is given by x + y + (xy/100). Use positive signs for increments and negative signs for decrements.

Product Rule in Percentages

If a final quantity is determined by the product of two variables (Z = A × B), the percentage change in Z equals the successive percentage changes applied to A and B.

Base Value Assumption

Assuming initial values as 100 makes calculating percentage increases or decreases highly straightforward, allowing avoidance of cumbersome variables and fractions.

questions.q: A shopkeeper marked the price 20% more than its cost price. If he allows a discount of 30%, then find his loss percent.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

We can use the successive percentage change formula: Net % Change = a + b + (a × b) / 100

Here, the markup percentage (a) = +20% and the discount percentage (b) = −30%.

Net % Change = 20 − 30 + (20 × −30) / 100

Net % Change = −10 − 6 = −16%

The negative sign indicates an overall loss of 16%.

∴ The correct answer is 16%.

Alternate Method

Given:

⇒ Markup Percentage = 20%

⇒ Discount Percentage = 30%



Calculations:

⇒ Let the Cost Price (CP) of the article be 100.

⇒ Marked Price (MP) = CP + 20% of CP = 100 + 20 = 120

⇒ Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price.

⇒ Selling Price (SP) = MP − 30% of MP

⇒ SP = 120 − (30 / 100 × 120) = 120 − 36 = 84

⇒ Since Selling Price is less than Cost Price, there is a loss.

⇒ Loss = CP − SP = 100 − 84 = 16

⇒ Loss Percentage = (Loss / CP) × 100 = (16 / 100) × 100 = 16%

∴ The correct answer is 16%.

Additional Information

Successive Discounts

If two successive discounts of a% and b% are given on an article, the single equivalent discount is calculated as: D = a + b − (a × b) / 100.

CP and MP Relationship

The direct ratio between Cost Price and Marked Price is given by the formula: CP / MP = (100 − Discount%) / (100 + Profit%). If there is a loss, use (100 − Loss%).

Dishonest Dealer Rule

When a shopkeeper claims to sell goods at Cost Price but uses a false weight, the actual profit percent is: Profit% = (Error / True Weight − Error) × 100.

Trigonometric Ratios

If x − 1/x = a, then x³ − 1/x³ = a³ + 3a.

⇒ (x − 1/x)² = 81

⇒ x − 1/x = ±9

⇒ x³ − 1/x³ = (x − 1/x)(x² + 1/x² + 1)

⇒ x³ − 1/x³ = 9 × (83 + 1)

⇒ x³ − 1/x³ = 9 × 84

⇒ x³ − 1/x³ = 756

∴ The correct answer is 756.

Reciprocal Identities

If x + 1/x = p, then x² + 1/x² = p² − 2 and x³ + 1/x³ = p³ − 3p.

Negative Reciprocal Identities

The difference of cubes formula is a³ − b³ = (a − b)(a² + b² + ab). Substituting 1/x for b gives the identity x³ − 1/x³ = (x − 1/x)(x² + 1/x² + 1).

⇒ Multiply the first ratio by 7 ⇒ A : B = (3 × 7) : (4 × 7) = 21 : 28

⇒ Multiply the second ratio by 4 ⇒ B : C = (7 × 4) : (10 × 4) = 28 : 40

⇒ Now, B is equal in both equations, allowing direct combination.

⇒ A : B : C = 21 : 28 : 40

∴ The correct answer is 21:28:40.

Additional Information

Compound Ratio

The compound ratio of two different ratios a : b and c : d is calculated by multiplying the antecedents together and consequents together as ac : bd.

Duplicate & Triplicate Ratio

The duplicate ratio of a : b is given by a² : b², and the triplicate ratio is given by a³ : b³.

Invertendo

If a : b = c : d, then according to the invertendo property, the inverse ratios are also equal, meaning b : a = d : c.

questions.q: If cos 24° = nm​ , then the value of (cosec 24° - cos 66°) is:

Given, cos 24° = m / n

Using complementary angles, cos 66° = cos(90° − 24°) = sin 24°

Expression: cosec 24° − cos 66° = 1 / sin 24° − sin 24° = (1 − sin² 24°) / sin 24° = cos² 24° / sin 24°

Since cos 24° = m / n, we get sin 24° = √(1 − m²/n²) = √(n² − m²) / n

⇒ Value = (m / n)² × [n / √(n² − m²)] = m² / [n√(n² − m²)]

∴ The correct answer is m² / [n√(n² − m²)].

questions.q: The circumference of the base of a cylindrical vessel is 44 cm and its height is 25 cm. How many liters of water can it hold? (Take pi = 722​)
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Radius (r) = Circumference ÷ 2π = 44 × (7/44) = 7 cm.

Volume in cm³ = π × r² × h = (22/7) × 7² × 25 = 3850 cm³.

Convert to liters (1 L = 1000 cm³): 3850 ÷ 1000 = 3.85 liters.

∴ The correct answer is 3.85 liters.

Alternate Method

Given:

Circumference of the base = 44 cm

Height of the cylinder (h) = 25 cm



Formula Used:

Circumference of base = 2πr

Volume of cylinder = πr²h

1 liter = 1000 cm³

Calculations:

⇒ 2 × (22/7) × r = 44

⇒ (44/7) × r = 44

⇒ r = 44 × (7/44)

⇒ r = 7 cm

⇒ Volume of cylinder = (22/7) × (7)² × 25

⇒ Volume = (22/7) × 49 × 25

⇒ Volume = 22 × 7 × 25

⇒ Volume = 154 × 25

⇒ Volume = 3850 cm³

⇒ Capacity in liters = 3850 ÷ 1000 = 3.85 liters

∴ The correct answer is 3.85 liters.

Additional Information

Total Surface Area of Cylinder

TSA = 2πr(r + h), where r is the radius of the base and h is the height.

Curved Surface Area of Cylinder

CSA = 2πrh. This represents the outer wall surface area, excluding the top and bottom circular faces.

Metric Volume Conversion

1 m³ = 1000 liters. Conversely, 1 liter = 1000 cm³ or 1000 ml.
